description: Labelled note content for the structure validator (Phase 8.5), used while tuning. Each line is '<code> | <text>' (I ingredient, S step, H heading, N note, O other; 'H+S' is a heading glued to a step); blank strings are blank lines, which drive the importer's DOM rules. Lines are written as the importer extracts them (the text of each en-note child).

notes.description: The stored dev note (American Beauty Venison Backstrap): clean blocks, and a sauce heading glued to its step.
lines: I | ¼ cup, plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
I | ½ cup American beautyberry jelly (may substitute currant, blackberry, or wild dewberry jelly)
I | Zest and juice of 1 orange
I | Zest and juice of 1 lemon
S | Dry-age the backstrap by placing it on a rack over a drip pan in the refrigerator for 24 – 48 hours.

S | When you are ready to cook, place the backstrap in a narrow baking dish and add ¼ cup of the oil, the vinegar, thyme, and salt. Using tongs, turn the meat to coat evenly with the marinade. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let sit at room temperature for 2 hours, turning the backstrap every 15 minutes so that all surfaces are evenly coated.
S | Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.

S | Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat, then add the backstrap and sear for 3 – 6 minutes, turning it with tongs every few minutes to sear evenly on all sides.

S | Place the backstrap in a baking dish and cook in the oven, uncovered, for 10 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 130 degrees. Remove from the oven, loosely tent with foil, and let the meat rest for 5 minutes to allow the juices to reabsorb.

H+S | For the Cumberland sauce: Combine all the ingredients in a small saucepan over medium-low heat and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce is reduced by half and thick enough to coat a spoon. Serve warm.
S | Cut venison into -inch-thick medallions, plate, and drizzle with Cumberland sauce.
